key_insight: TSGSurv connects faithful generation of censored time-to-event data to consistent Cox model estimates, while showing that valid inference requires more than distributional fidelity.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports synthetic survival data for biomedical data sharing, clinical trial simulation, and digital twins, with corrections for downstream statistical inference.
method: Use a two-stage framework to jointly generate observed times and covariates conditional on event status.
Establish distributional convergence rates and conditions for consistent Cox coefficient estimates.
Apply variance correction and distribution calibration to recover valid inference for the original data.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports extensive simulations and two real-data applications, but provides no quantitative performance results.
watch_item: Naive inference from synthetic data can be unreliable; consistency depends on stated conditions, and valid inference requires the proposed corrections.
paper_title: Faithful Generative Modeling for Censored Time-to-Event Data: From Distributional Fidelity to Statistical Inference
